items.title: Lillie Delk Christian Interview, 1961-04-25
items.q: The interviewer states: 'Then Louie Armstrong finally with Jimmy Noon, Earl Hines, Manson... Manson Kara happened to be on banjo for that date.' The interviewee confirms participation in these sessions: 'Well Earl Hines played for me when I played when I was with Louis... And I had all those records

ctx.x: That name sounds very familiar. More so than the others. Well uh. Yeah. The only reason I mention uh. Nicholas is that he played with Richard M Jones but the style of it makes it a little

difficult because uh playing clarinet softly to an accompaniment uh it's not quite as easy to identify the clarinet as if he's playing some sort of. Uh huh. And then a little later again Jimmy Noon and Johnny Sincere they say in December of that year. So every few months why you had a couple sides. Yeah. Coming up didn't you? Then Louie Armstrong finally with Jimmy Noon, Earl Hines, Manson, Manson, Manson, Manson, and Manson. And then Louie Armstrong finally with Jimmy Noon, Earl Hines, Manson, Manson, Manson,…
